findings.practical_consequence: A planner would treat successful run close as a reliably automatic learning trigger, although capture can be disabled, skipped when context is absent, or fail after the run is already committed; those cases materially change whether a successful path enters discovery.
evidence: Required behavior: requirements.json:3-16 requires the exact current trigger and observation boundary, while requirements.json:51-64 requires every automatic, opt-in, and manual success-learning transition.

Demonstrated omitted behavior: scripts/work_memory.py:1998-2025 commits run_closed first, invokes the observer only for enabled mode or auto mode with operation context and MK_SEQUENCE_OBSERVER_DISABLED != 1, catches every observer exception, and surfaces DISABLED or OBSERVER_FAILED without rolling back the terminal run.

Candidate omission: candidate-round-1.json requirement_statuses for CUR-001 and CUR-003 and research_markdown sections CUR-001/CUR-003 describe post-close automatic capture but do not state the mode, environment, context prerequisites, committed-before-observation ordering, or failure degradation.

findings.practical_consequence: Planning from the candidate would recreate measurement capabilities that already exist and would not clearly distinguish reusable current correction/outcome metrics from the genuinely missing sequence-learning denominators and lifecycle metrics.
evidence: Required behavior: requirements.json:123-135 asks which outcome metrics currently exist, and requirements.json:333-344 defines the additional future learning-loop metrics.

Demonstrated current behavior: scripts/work_memory.py:2050-2082 computes closed-run, pass, first-pass-success, corrections-per-run, repeated-blocker, same-path-verification, and duration metrics with explicit denominators; scripts/work_memory.py:2096-2148 computes trend and before/after correction-bundle change effects.

Candidate contradiction: candidate-round-1.json records CUR-006 research_value.learning_effectiveness_metrics as false, even though its prose only supports the narrower conclusion that silver/gold lifecycle, eligible-observation, reuse, false-match, evidence-hold, and known-wrong-step-recurrence metrics are absent.

findings.practical_consequence: A planner cannot assign a concrete producer and enforcement boundary for each missing action class because file edits, browser actions, generic MCP/tool calls, subagent actions, and reasoning self-reports are collapsed into one unsupported statement instead of being traced individually.
evidence: Required behavior: requirements.json:146-160 requires each named action class to be mapped to its producer, durable record, observer consumer, enforcement point, or confirmed absence.

Demonstrated implemented side: scripts/sequence_checked_exec.py:38-108 is the only repository producer joining guard, execution_claimed, shell-false argv dispatch, and execution_returned; scripts/sequence_observer.py:130-196 reconstructs candidates only from operation context plus those claim/return pairs.
Demonstrated remote side: mcp-agents-workflow/src/workflow_orch/cli/base.py:50-78 exposes aggregate invocation response fields rather than canonical ordered action events.

Candidate insufficiency: candidate-round-1.json CUR-007 reports one argv row, one aggregate remote row, and a single 'other_action_classes' absence. Its evidence index contains no per-class producer/consumer trace or bounded authoritative-root absence result for file-edit, browser, MCP/tool, subagent, and reasoning classes.
findings.evidence_limitation: The accessible roots are sufficient to perform and index the missing per-class trace; the current candidate has not done so.

findings.practical_consequence: Without new authoritative producers, successful or failed non-argv model actions cannot enter the learning loop and unsupported surfaces cannot fail visibly.
evidence: requirements.json:170-183 requires a named producer, safe event, stable identity, outcome link, and observer consumer for every in-scope action class.

scripts/sequence_checked_exec.py:38-108 and scripts/sequence_observer.py:130-196 establish the reusable argv producer/consumer pattern; mcp-agents-workflow/src/workflow_orch/cli/base.py:50-78 establishes the current aggregate-only remote boundary.

findings.practical_consequence: A matching registered sequence is not guaranteed to intercept effect dispatch, so the model can still improvise before selection and guard enforcement begin.
evidence: requirements.json:194-206 requires a matching gold sequence to be selected before dispatch.

scripts/work_memory.py:1314-1383 selects by operation kind, optional explicit sequence ID, or verified blocker fingerprint and returns ambiguity instead of intercepting dispatch; scripts/sequence_guard.py:568-729 enforces only after selection and activation.

scripts/sequence_observer.py:130-196 and 534-584 build and compare full identities only after a completed run, so the planner must define a distinct pre-dispatch applicability contract compatible with the proven post-run identity.

findings.practical_consequence: A proven unrecorded success can become a discovery, but it does not autonomously traverse qualification, promotion, registered verification, and later pre-dispatch reuse.
evidence: requirements.json:217-229 and 471-484 require canonical success capture and a lifecycle-spanning reuse proof.
scripts/sequence_observer.py:1104-1127 can propose/bootstrap a discovery after close; scripts/discovery_promotion_lifecycle.py:380-415 exposes an explicitly driven lifecycle controller.
tests/test_sequence_observer_end_to_end.py is indexed as E-E2E and demonstrates the lifecycle only when its stages are explicitly invoked.

findings.practical_consequence: A model saying that its own action caused a failure cannot currently produce an authoritative repair candidate or prevent that step from recurring without a separate governed action/failure/correction join.
evidence: requirements.json:240-275 requires self-diagnosis to remain a signal while grounded action, failure, blocker, replacement, and successor evidence supply causal authority.

scripts/blocker_catalog.py:20-76 creates normalized blocker fingerprints tied to run, lineage, step, and surface, while scripts/work_memory.py correction and successor contracts govern replacement evidence.
No current observer input contract accepts a model self-diagnosis event; scripts/sequence_observer.py:130-196 consumes operation, execution, verification, blocker, and correction ledger events.

findings.practical_consequence: Correcting a registered sequence does not create a quarantined, independently requalified replacement version with an atomic selector cutover, so old and corrected eligibility cannot be managed as immutable versions.
evidence: requirements.json:286-299 requires versioned replacement, auditability, quarantine, requalification, registered verification, and atomic cutover.

scripts/discovery_promotion_lifecycle.py exposes registered correction and successor verification, while scripts/sequence_promote.py:222-384 materializes discovery-to-registration without a registered replacement-version identity.
scripts/work_memory.py:2133-2147 compares old and new bundle hashes but does not define selector-visible immutable sequence versions.

findings.practical_consequence: The system lacks canonical selectable lifecycle levels and learning-loop denominators, so it cannot prove silver growth, gold reuse, false-match control, or falling wrong-step recurrence.
evidence: requirements.json:310-344 defines silver/gold transition intent and the required effectiveness metric set.
operations/sequences/SEQUENCES.md defines registered and discovery catalog states without silver/gold fields.

scripts/work_memory.py:2050-2148 provides reusable run/correction metrics but not eligible-observation, silver conversion, gold reuse, false-match, evidence-hold, or known-wrong-step-recurrence contracts.

findings.practical_consequence: Separate sequence and workflow stores can resume independently without a shared current-version and conflict contract, allowing duplicate candidates, lost corrections, or stale selection across runs and branches.
evidence: requirements.json:378-391 and 448-460 require one durable branch-safe ownership model and immutable versioned feedback consumption.
scripts/work_memory.py:2158-2203 merges event ledgers by event identity and rejects conflicts but owns only the sequence ledger boundary.

mcp-agents-workflow/src/workflow_orch/workflow_state_store.py is indexed as E-WORKFLOW-STATE and persists separate per-run workflow/phase JSON state without sequence candidate/version synchronization.
